name: Disruption of 1843
summary: The walkout of about a third of the Church of Scotland's ministers, led by Thomas Chalmers, to form the Free Church of Scotland over the right of congregations to reject ministers imposed by patrons.

start.label: General Assembly passes the Veto Act, letting congregations reject patrons' nominees

end.label: About 450 ministers walk out of the General Assembly to form the Free Church

key_dates.label: Court of Session rules against the church in the Auchterarder case
General Assembly adopts the Claim of Right; the government rejects it

background.text: Under the Patronage Act of 1712, landowners and the crown could present ministers to parishes; evangelicals argued congregations should have a say and that civil courts had no power over spiritual matters.

happened.text: In the 'Ten Years' Conflict' the civil courts, upheld by the House of Lords, ruled that the church's Veto Act was illegal and ordered presbyteries to admit patrons' nominees.
On 18 May 1843 the retiring moderator read a protest and led some 450 ministers out of St Andrew's Church in Edinburgh; they formed the Free Church of Scotland under Thomas Chalmers.
The ministers gave up their churches, manses, and salaries; within a few years the Free Church had built hundreds of churches, schools, and manses by voluntary giving.

participants.name: Thomas Chalmers
participants.role: Leader of the evangelical party and first moderator of the Free Church

participants.name: David Welsh
participants.role: Retiring moderator who read the protest

participants.name: Robert Peel
participants.role: Prime minister whose government refused the Claim of Right

outcomes.text: Patronage was abolished in 1874; most of the Free Church united with the United Presbyterians in 1900 and then with the Church of Scotland in 1929, while a minority continued as the Free Church of Scotland.

condemnations.by: General Assembly of the Church of Scotland (evangelical majority)
condemnations.reason: Seven ministers of Strathbogie deposed for obeying the civil court rather than the church
condemnations.status: Restored by the post-Disruption assembly in 1843

persecution.title: Refusal of building sites to the Free Church
persecution.summary: Some landowners, including the Duke of Buccleuch at first, refused to sell or lease land for Free Church buildings, forcing congregations to meet in the open air, in tents, or, at Strontian, in a floating church moored in Loch Sunart. A parliamentary committee investigated in 1847.

responsible.name: Landowners opposed to the Free Church

sources.citation: Stewart J. Brown, Thomas Chalmers and the Godly Commonwealth in Scotland. Oxford: Oxford University Press, 1982.
